The second au
arxiv-2007-06161.creator: John Bamberg and James Evans
arxiv-2007-06161.description: Abstract . A generalised quadrangle is a point-line incidence geometry 𝒢 \mathcal{G} such that: (i) any two points lie on at most one line, and (ii) given a line L L and a point p p not incident with L L , there is a unique point on L L collinear with p p .

arxiv-2108-11347.title: The Next 700 Program Transformers
arxiv-2108-11347.creator: G.W. Hamilton
arxiv-2108-11347.description: Abstract In this paper, we describe a hierarchy of program transformers in which the transformer at each level of the hierarchy builds on top of those at lower levels. The program transformer at level 1 of the hierarchy corresponds to positive supercompilation, and that at level 2 corresponds to distillation. We prove that the transformers at each level terminate.

arxiv-2112-09916.title: Time series analysis of friction force at self-affine mode of ice surface softening
arxiv-2112-09916.creator: A. V. Khomenko ? , ?, D. T. Logvinenko ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}
arxiv-2112-09916.description: Abstract The self-affine mode of ice softening during friction is investigated within the rheological model for viscoelastic medium approximation. The different modes of ice rubbing, determined by formation of surface liquid-like layer, are studied. The analysis of time series of friction force is carried out, namely Fourier analysis, construction of autocorrelation and difference autocorrelation functions.

arxiv-2202-08317.title: Locating fast-varying line disturbances with the frequency mismatch RD was supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation under grant P400P2_194359.
arxiv-2202-08317.creator: Robin Delabays, 1 Laurent Pagnier, 2 and Melvyn Tyloo 3
arxiv-2202-08317.description: Abstract In an attempt to provide an efficient method for line disturbance identification in complex networks of diffusively coupled agents, we recently proposed to leverage the frequency mismatch . The frequency mismatch filters out the intricate combination of interactions induced by the network structure and quantifies to what extent the trajectory of each agent is affected by the disturbance.

arxiv-2205-01270.title: A Search for Annihilating Dark Matter in 47 Tucanae and Omega Centauri
arxiv-2205-01270.creator: Lister Staveley-Smith, Emma Bond, Kenji Bekki, Tobias Westmeier
arxiv-2205-01270.description: Abstract A plausible formation scenario for the Galactic globular clusters 47 Tucanae (47 Tuc) and Omega Centauri ( ω \omega Cen) is that they are tidally stripped remnants of dwarf galaxies, in which case they are likely to have retained a fraction of their dark matter cores.

arxiv-2208-07646.title: Indirect X-ray photodesorption of 15 N 2 and 13 CO from mixed and layered ices
arxiv-2208-07646.creator: R. Basalgète, D. Torres-Díaz, A. Lafosse, L. Amiaud, G. Féraud, P. Jeseck, L. Philippe, X. Michaut, J-H. Fillion, M. Bertin
arxiv-2208-07646.description: Abstract X-ray photodesorption yields of 15 N 2 and 13 CO are derived as a function of the incident photon energy near the N ( ∼ \sim 400 eV) and O K-edge ( ∼ \sim 500 eV) for pure 15 N 2 ice and mixed 13 CO: 15 N 2 ices.

arxiv-2301-01190.title: Carbon in solution and the Charpy impact performance of medium Mn steels Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2301-01190.creator: TWJ Kwok, FF Worsnop, JO Douglas, D Dye
arxiv-2301-01190.description: Abstract Carbon is a well known austenite stabiliser and can be used to alter the stacking fault energy and stability against martensitic transformation in medium Mn steels, producing a range of deformation mechanisms such as the Transformation Induced Plasticity (TRIP) or combined Twinning and Transformation Induced Plasticity (TWIP + + TRIP) effects.

arxiv-2302-03568.title: Quantum dynamics of coupled excitons and phonons in chain-like systems: tensor train approaches and higher-order propagators
arxiv-2302-03568.creator: Patrick Gelß, Sebastian Matera, Rupert Klein, Burkhard Schmidt
arxiv-2302-03568.description: Abstract We investigate tensor-train approaches to the solution of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for chain-like quantum systems with on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions only. Using efficient low-rank tensor train representations, we aim at reducing memory consumption and computational costs. As an example, coupled excitons and phonons modeled in terms of Fröhlich-Holstein type Hamiltonians are studied here.

arxiv-2306-16401.title: Pumping with symmetry
arxiv-2306-16401.creator: J. A. Iglesias Martínez, M. Kadic, V. Laude, E. Prodan
arxiv-2306-16401.description: Abstract Re-configurable materials and meta-materials can jump between space symmetry classes during their deformations. Here, we introduce the concept of singular symmetry enhancement, which refers to an abrupt jump to a higher symmetry class accompanied by an un-avoidable reduction in the number of dispersion bands of the excitations of the material.

arxiv-2307-12798.title: RRAML: Reinforced Retrieval Augmented Machine Learning
arxiv-2307-12798.creator: Andrea Bacciu, Florin Cuconasu, Federico Siciliano, Fabrizio Silvestri, Nicola Tonellotto, Giovanni Trappolini, [2ex] {surname}@diag.uniroma1.it, nicola.tonellotto@unipi.it
arxiv-2307-12798.description: Abstract The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized machine learning and related fields, showcasing remarkable abilities in comprehending, generating, and manipulating human language. However, their conventional usage through API-based text prompt submissions imposes certain limitations in terms of context constraints and external source availability.

arxiv-2404-07925.title: Non-perturbative quantum gravity denounces singular Black Holes
arxiv-2404-07925.creator: Alexey S. Koshelev, Anna Tokareva
arxiv-2404-07925.description: Abstract Although General Relativity predicts the presence of a singularity inside of a Black Hole, it is not a complete theory of gravity. A real structure of a Black Hole interior near an expected singularity depends on the UV completion of gravity.

arxiv-2410-17956.title: Radio sensitivity to a new population of millisecond pulsars in the Sagittarius Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxy
arxiv-2410-17956.creator: Lucia Gebauer Werner, Oscar Macias, Christoph Weniger
arxiv-2410-17956.description: Abstract Observations with the Fermi Gamma-Ray Space Telescope reveal an excess of extended gamma-ray emission likely caused by an undiscovered population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the core of the Sagittarius dwarf spheroidal galaxy (Sgr dSph). However, additional evidence, such as multi-wavelength searches, is necessary to confirm this theory.

arxiv-2501-14046.title: LLM-guided Instance-level Image Manipulation with Diffusion U-Net Cross-Attention Maps
arxiv-2501-14046.creator: Andrey Palaev, Adil Khan, Syed M. Ahsan Kazmi
arxiv-2501-14046.description: Abstract The advancement of text-to-image synthesis has introduced powerful generative models capable of creating realistic images from textual prompts. However, precise control over image attributes remains challenging, especially at the instance level. While existing methods offer some control through fine-tuning or auxiliary information, they often face limitations in flexibility and accuracy.

arxiv-2507-14394.title: An Effective Reflection Mode Measurement for Hanger-Coupled Microwave Resonators
arxiv-2507-14394.creator: John R. Pitten, Nicholas Materise, Wei-Ren Syong, Jorge Ramirez, Douglas Bennett, Corey Rae H. McRae
arxiv-2507-14394.description: Abstract Superconducting microwave resonators are used to study two-level system (TLS) loss in superconducting quantum devices. Fano asymmetry, characterized by a nonzero asymmetry angle ϕ \phi in the diameter correction method (DCM), results from the coupling schemes used to measure these devices, including the commonly used hanger method.

plos-pone-0004779.description: PLOS ONE research article. The specification and differentiation of dentate gyrus granule neurons in the hippocampus require temporally and spatially coordinated actions of both intrinsic and extrinsic molecules. The basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor Neurogenin2 (Ngn2) and NeuroD1 are key regulat

pmc-10737912.title: SUCCESSFUL CARE CONFERENCES: NURSING HOME STAFF, PERSONS WITH DEMENTIA AND CAREGIVER PERSPECTIVES
pmc-10737912.creator: Gail Towsley, Linda Edelman, Shelby Montez
pmc-10737912.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Work demands of the care team, time constraints, and a lack of guidance from the regulatory environment often result in short, perfunctory mandated quarterly care conferences (e.g., care plan meetings) that lack focus on resident preferences. Me & My Wishes is a video recording approach for documenting, viewing, listening, and discussing nursing home (NH) residents’ living with dementia preferences for daily and end-of-life in care conferences.

pmc-12504697.title: The 2023 drought in West Africa and associated vulnerability to food insecurity
pmc-12504697.creator: Vincent Ondima Kongo, Nkongho Ayuketang Arreyndip
pmc-12504697.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The return of El Niño in 2023 brought record global temperatures, an increase in forest fires, floods, heatwaves, and intense and severe droughts. How the climate of 2023 affected agricultural activities in West Africa is not yet known. This paper analyses the changes in the patterns of local climate variables during the planting season and the potential consequences for agricultural productivity in West Africa.

pmc-12569630.title: ﻿Lysimachia barcae (Primulaceae), a new endemic shrub from Wainiha, Kaua‘i, Hawaiian Islands
pmc-12569630.creator: Kenneth R Wood, Warren L Wagner, Susan Fawcett, Scott Heintzman
pmc-12569630.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ﻿AbstractA new endemic species of Lysimachia from Kaua‘i, Hawaiian Islands, is described and illustrated with notes on its distribution, ecology, conservation status and phylogenetic relationships. A modification to the existing key for Hawaiian Lysimachia is provided.

pmc-13261058.title: An Open Non-Invasive EEG Dataset for Spontaneous Auditory Attention Switch Decoding
pmc-13261058.creator: Xuefei Wang, Yuting Ding, Yueting Ban, Lei Wang, Fei Chen
pmc-13261058.description: Auditory brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) based on non-invasive electrodes offer significant potential for advancing the understanding of selective auditory attention mechanisms and enabling natural human–computer interaction. Despite growing interest in auditory attention research, publicly available datasets focused on spontaneous auditory attention switching remain limited, particularly those with high-quality electroencephalography (EEG) recordings in realistic listening environments.

pmc-13386788.title: Effects of weather factors and maternal characteristics on preterm birth: a six-year retrospective study
pmc-13386788.creator: Büsra Korkmaz, Fatma Ocakoglu, Ayse Aydın
pmc-13386788.description: BackgroundPreterm birth represents a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and fatality globally. Recent research has increasingly focused on the potential influence of meteorological and ecological variables on adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly in the context of environmental change. Despite this attention, the evidence is still inconsistent, and there is a paucity of data from humid subtropical regions.

pmc-13470007.title: Glutamatergic signaling underlies brain structural organization for mathematical and reading abilities in children
pmc-13470007.creator: Yuan Zhang, Hyesang Chang, Dawlat El-Said, Vinod Menon
pmc-13470007.description: The neurochemical mechanisms underlying individual differences in children’s mathematical and reading abilities remain largely unknown. Here we investigate how neurotransmitter systems relate to brain structural organization supporting these abilities in two independent cohorts of children (N = 991). We mapped brain-wide structural phenotypes associated with academic performance onto a comprehensive PET atlas of 19 neurotransmitter receptors and transporters.

pmc-13482293.title: Engineering trispecific IL-2 receptor agonistic antibodies through geometry optimization for enhanced Treg targeting
pmc-13482293.creator: Valentina Lykhopiy, Emilie Pollenus, Laurie Rangan, Michelle Stakenborg, Tugsan Tezil, Michiel Varheust, Giel Tanghe, Nina Lambrechts, Vanshika Malviya, Eva De Langhe, Gianluca Matteoli, Christophe Blanchetot, Luc Van Rompaey, Susan M Schlenner
pmc-13482293.description: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are central to maintaining immune tolerance, and their selective activation via interleukin-2 (IL-2) signaling presents a promising therapeutic strategy for autoimmune diseases and transplant rejection. Here, we develop IL-2 receptor (IL-2R) agonists, employing trispecific antibodies that simultaneously engage all three IL-2R subunits.
